fields.description: Which reader this checkpoint belongs to: 'journald' or 'authlog'. One row per source, so switching sources and switching back resumes where each left off instead of re-reading.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: Clear this to park a source without deleting its position. Useful when pinning to the other source temporarily.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: 'Source Unavailable' means the log could not be read at all — usually a permissions problem. 'Cursor Lost' means the journal rotated past our stored position; the reader restarts from Bootstrap Hours and dedup absorbs the overlap, so no action is needed.
fields.label: Last Run Status
fields.options:
Never Run
OK
No New Records
Cursor Lost
Source Unavailable
Error

fields.description: journald's opaque __CURSOR for the last record consumed. Stored here rather than in journalctl's own --cursor-file so it is visible in the desk, included in site backups, and cannot drift out of step with the rows that were actually committed.
fields.label: Journal Cursor

fields.description: The auth.log file this offset refers to.
fields.label: File Path

fields.description: Inode of the file at the time the offset was taken. This is how log rotation is detected: a changed inode means the file we were reading is now auth.log.1, and its tail must be drained before starting the new file at zero.
fields.label: Inode

fields.description: How far into the file we have read. Only ever advanced past a line that ended in a newline, so a half-written line is never treated as consumed.
fields.label: Byte Offset

fields.description: Fingerprint of the first bytes of the auth.log, as '<bytes>:<sha1>'. Appends never change a file's head, so a changed fingerprint means the file was replaced — which catches the case where the filesystem reuses the inode and the size check is fooled as well.
fields.label: File Signature

fields.description: Records already present, recognised by their dedup hash. A non-zero value after a Cursor Lost run is expected and is the safety net working.
fields.label: Records Skipped

fields.description: sshd or sudo lines that matched no rule. This should be zero. A persistent non-zero count means this server emits a message format the parser has never seen — check Last Error for a sample and add a rule with a fixture.
fields.label: Records Unparsed
